newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission to consider paper on olive oil.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission to consider paper on olive oil.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to be asked to adopt a discussion paper on the future of the European Union's olive oil regime next Wednesday, an official said.

The paper, prepared by farm Commisisoner Franz Fischler, warns of the danger of over-production because of General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) world market export limits and large numbers of newly planted groves which have yet to begin producing.
"A reflection paper is ready to be put to the Commission outlining possible changes to the olive oil regime," the official added.
The paper presents generalised fraud as a root problem of the current regime, which offers flat-rate aid payments to small producers and different production aids for large producers and crushers.
"There is an obvious danger of payment of subsidies twice since small producers sell their crops to large organisations which then exaggerate their own production figures," the official said.
Fischler has suggested two possibilities -- the continuation of the present system or payment by tree calculated on the historic yield per tree.
On so-called consumption aid, used to promote sales of olive oil within the EU, the paper says this should be increased or abolished, the official added.
